gen-dafont-groovy-gf-hind-vadodara: Groovy's c nearly seals shut, leaving a thin slit, and its loosely spaced lowercase feels funky. Hind Vadodara is the opposite: rounded shapes with wide terminal gaps and a stroke that never changes thickness.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-karla: Modern and approachable, the body text has a gaping c and a middle band so large the lines look stocky. Karla would keep paragraphs feeling sturdy and open, a foil to Groovy's nearly shut, funky letters.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri feels approachable, with rounded letters that stay inviting beneath a skyward x-height line, far from Groovy's nearly shut c. Page after page of it would flow along without snagging.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-krub: Groovy's c nearly closes into a narrow slit. Krub, the sans-serif body, has a pronounced x-height and pen-lifted curves that leave the loop unfinished, the reverse of that sealed-up c.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend-deca: Groovy squeezes its c to a narrow slit and spaces its lowercase loosely, giving it a funky grin. But Lexend Deca draws a plain, unshaded line with terminals that stop short of curling back.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-liter: Liter has no stroke contrast at all, lowercase with great vertical presence, and wide mouths on its round forms. Groovy supplies the funk, Liter supplies the structure and the open curves.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-mada: Approachable and modern, the body text lets its curves refuse to close, with a towering midzone. Mada, set beside Groovy's nearly sealed c, makes those open curves feel all the more generous.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-michroma: Michroma gives each letter a wide berth on both sides. Its curves leave daylight like a rope's open bight, so paragraphs would move slowly and spaciously, quite unlike Groovy's twine-pressed funk.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-mozilla-text: Groovy pinches its c to a narrow slit, and its loosely tracked lowercase makes a line feel like following a single thread. Groovy charms, while Mozilla Text lends bold-looking lowercase and flared terminals.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-nata-sans: Funky meets tidy: Groovy's c nearly closes, while Nata Sans keeps a large central band in the text line. And its wide, unclosed curves, drawn with a technical pen's steadiness, would carry paragraphs along without fuss.
